reason: The cited evidence shows that KKR-CPA can model HEA structural properties and that a related HEA exhibits intermediate electron-phonon coupling, but neither passage provides direct support for the key premises that randomness optimizes coupling or that clustering disrupts it. The link between atomic configuration and superconducting parameters is not addressed in the cited studies.
premises: Fully random atomic distribution maximizes favorable density-of-states at EF and electron-phonon coupling
Nanoscale atomic clustering disrupts optimal density-of-states and phonon modes
KKR-CPA and DFT can reliably model electron-phonon coupling and Tc in HEAs
The specific HEA (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 behaves similarly to Nb0.34Ti0.33Zr0.14Ta0.11Hf0.08
